title: SKILL-BACKOFF: per-cell skill estimates with and without back-off; which hierarchy makes them best (MATH, MMLU-Pro, BBH, MMLU; exploratory, WORK rows; test 2 of D-2026-11-02-1, run under D-2026-11-03-1)
question: Can a model's skill be read reliably at fine granularity, and which hierarchy makes those per-cell estimates best? Per-model per-cell skill estimates p[c, m] at V0's leaf granularity (NEST-METER's level L, matched cell counts), scored by held-out log-loss on WORK rows; arms LABELS, TREE-RAW, TREE-BO, BKMA-BO, KF-BO, RND-BO (TREE-BL, BKMA-BL, BKMA-SM descriptive); contrasts Z_hier = BKMA-BO - TREE-BO, Z_bo = TREE-BO - TREE-RAW, Z_nest = KF-BO - BKMA-BO, V_* = arm - LABELS, B_lab = LABELS-b - LABELS; words at 3 SE_word = max(SE_content, SE_leaf), SE_label beside (plan sections 1, 3, 5, 7).

sentence_of_record: On WORK rows of MATH, MMLU-Pro, BBH and MMLU (per-cell skill estimates at V0's leaf granularity, held-out log-loss, words at 3 SE_word = max(SE_content, SE_leaf)), shrinking per-model leaf rates toward the label predicts held-out WORK responses better than the raw leaf rates on MATH, BBH and MMLU (Z_bo BETTER; MMLU-Pro z 2.47 NEITHER); which hierarchy the estimates back off along (V0 vs nested bisecting k-means) is not detected (Z_hier NEITHER; MDE80 0.75 / 2.13 / 0.78 / 4.54), nor flat KF vs nested BKMA (Z_nest NEITHER); random cells of V0's sizes carry nothing; the backbone dwarfs every cell effect (B_lab +47 to +207, z >= 9.7) [EXPLORATORY, adjudicates nothing; POSTRUN 59520e3f: Q1 (MEDIUM) on MATH the raw leaf rate is worse than the label rate, on MMLU better (label SE NEITHER), NEITHER on MMLU-Pro and BBH; Q2 (MEDIUM) the back-off gain is shrinkage toward the label, the internal levels not shown to help, so Z_hier and Z_nest are 'not detected under one common tau'; Q3 (MEDIUM) V_kf BETTER on MATH and MMLU-Pro is thin (z 3.11 / 3.03 at KF-cell SE; label SE NEITHER) and not a cells comparison; never 'equal' hierarchies, 'k-means cells beat the tree's cells', 'the tree's internal levels help', or any per-cell board, interval or profile]
